Triage: AsyncAPI React 3.1.6 and Lyxa core 1.0.201

AsyncAPI React: BENIGN. npm registry release bytes match the supplied SHA256.
The UI loads caller-provided specifications, parses AsyncAPI/OpenAPI/Avro/
protobuf schemas, renders markdown, and sanitizes HTML with DOMPurify.
Browser bundles include Ajv schema compilation, Avro VM compilation and
Long integer-arithmetic WebAssembly. Its 286-byte embedded module was
extracted and inspected with rizin and its section layout decoded: six
arithmetic exports, no imports, memory or table section. Highlight.js registers the bash grammar;
this does not execute bash. No install-time payload or covert network sink
was found. Likely label cause: bundled minification, code generation, and
network/parser capabilities were mistaken for a loader.

Lyxa core: BENIGN (insecure application library). bootstrapCore is exported,
not automatically called on import. registerLibraries initializes Redis,
Secret Manager, MongoDB, Firebase, Twilio, maps, logging and an AMQP event bus.
Default credentials point to the author's backends. Redis and Firebase
options can be overridden, but the AMQP broker and GCP Secret Manager
credentials are hardcoded. Incoming JSON is passed only to subscriber
methods registered through application decorators; network input does not
choose a method name or execute source/shell commands. Sending application
events and accessing the application's databases are intentional functions.
Five embedded PEM private keys and shared broker/Redis credentials expose
these systems. Credential exposure is suspicious, not proof of theft,
backdoor intent, or arbitrary code execution. This explains the external
MAL-2026-13434 classification. Its cited reference version and hash differ
from the supplied archive, but the same insecure design is present here.
https://osv.dev/vulnerability/MAL-2026-13434

Referenced Mongoose 8.24.5, pino-pretty 13.2.0 and libphonenumber-js 1.13.15
were downloaded from npm, scanned, and inspected. Their package entrypoints,
dependencies and scripts support ODM, log formatting, and phone validation.
No unexplained payload was found. Lyxa's registry version now returns 404.
Referenced AsyncAPI repository and IANA media-type pages were also inspected.
No service was authenticated to using exposed credentials.

Rule changes preserve neutral network/execution/crypto signals. Generic
Firebase dependency metadata moved out of Fetch Coder identity. AMQP moved
from local IPC to network pub/sub; named consumers were updated. Payment
field syntax no longer asserts a browser or credential theft. The redundant
core-module dependency composite was merged with its canonical observation,
with its exclusions retained on objective consumers. Ancestor YAML selectors
were searched; no broad IPC parent selector required membership changes.
Simple Icons identity no longer matches arbitrary repeated title fields.
A libphonenumber import no longer claims a vendored bundle; its source-map
marker moved from the ECMAScript bucket to the parsing-library identity.
Positive and near-miss controls cover keys, process calls, unit paths,
click attributes, application enums, product identity, dependency metadata,
AMQP URLs and payment fields. No live service secrets are stored in fixtures;
the fixture private key was generated solely for this test.

Limits: the scanner reports flow-graph/call/query limits in some large bundles.
Those behaviors were reviewed in source. binwalk was unavailable in this
session; JavaScript source and parser facts were used for package logic.
Rizin recognized the embedded WebAssembly but warned about its register/
calling-convention support. Verdicts apply to these supplied archives, not all
versions or the current state of their cloud services.
